triage.note: D7, both halves of the postmortem's trust amplifier. PANEL: `doc_status` and the warnings list live in the top banner and the side panel showed `conf 0.95` beside neither — postmortem §2, 'during a demo, the panel is the product'. Pinned as an ADJACENCY rather than as a question about the file: every live interpolation of `it.confidence` must sit where the pinned marker would start and must be followed IMMEDIATELY by `${docQual()}${itemQual(it)}`. PR #53 corrected this sentence twice. Round 0 ended it 'so a bare number is unrepresentable' and three of round 1's six findings were attacks through that word; round 1's replacement claimed 'no live interpolation of `it.confidence` renders without the pinned qualifier' and round 2 falsified that too. What the check asserts is now stated in `ceiling` as text it reads rather than as behaviour it prevents. The adjacency alone proved nothing about whether the qualifier RUNS (an early `if(true) return "";` left every pinned line intact below it as dead code and passed), nor about whether the banner strip is ever CALLED, nor about a site spelled `confidence ${it.confidence ?? "—"}` that the old literal `conf ${` scan could not see. So the three helper bodies are now pinned WHOLE via `bodies`, the call is pinned inside the banner assignment that makes it, and the scan looks for the FIELD rather than for one spelling of its label. The `boilerplate_plumbing` allow-list records why (PR #27 R5/R6): a question about a hop is answerable by a broken hop, and a list of forbidden shapes only bans the ones someone already thought of. `min_conf_sites` 2 is the anti-vacuity floor — the sidebar badge and the pane header each print one, and deleting a site is not a way to qualify it. The wire pins fix WHAT the qualifier reads: the response's own `doc_status` (the same read-at-request-time rule S8 gave the pane header) and the item's own `evidence.warnings`, which IS validate.py `score()`'s `hits` list, so the panel names exactly the codes that cost this item WARN_PENALTY and inherits ADR-018's exclusion of `expected_item_missing` instead of re-deriving a second definition in the display layer. BANNER: `unattributed_content` already computes the document-coverage figure and buries it in a warning row (postmortem §8 gap 1); `coverageStrip` surfaces it in the banner with validate.py's own caveat attached. `must_not_say` forbids the inversion that caveat exists to prevent — interior gaps are NOT counted, so `100 - outside` is not the attributed share and a banner publishing it would overstate coverage by exactly the uncounted gaps. Display layer only: `extract_items` output is untouched and the envelope half (a coverage field plus an escalation threshold) is D8's row. PR #53 R3 also split the badge class: `lo` keeps its pre-D7 meaning (amber TEXT = this item's own validators fired) and the document-level qualifier gets `docw` (amber BORDER), because folding both into `lo` repainted all 23 jpm-2024 badges identically and erased the one signal that finds item 15. The `flag` expression is a wire pin so that split is a pinned decision rather than an incidental one. PR #53 R7 renamed the banner label from 'document coverage:' to 'unattributed content:' — the figure measures NON-coverage, and a label reading 'coverage' over a bolded 73% is the same inversion `must_not_say` already forbids in arithmetic form; the old label is now itself forbidden. PR #53 round 2 closed the two remaining mechanism gaps and stopped restating the guarantee in a falsifiable form. The gaps: `_js_block` reads the FIRST `function <fn>(` while JS runs the LAST, so a hoisted `function docQual(){ return ""; }` stub left the pinned body byte-equal, won at runtime and restored the bare `conf 0.95` on all 20 cvx-2015 badges with the gate at 61/61 and 124/124 — each pinned name must now be declared exactly once; and the round-1 banner pin was only the assignment's RHS tail, so moving that tail onto a dead local passed — the pin now carries `$("#banner").innerHTML =`. The scan also moved from interpolations the field STARTS to the interpolation that ENCLOSES each mention, because `conf ${esc(it.confidence)}` names the field, prints a bare number, started nothing, and is the plausible next edit: every sibling badge in that template literal is already `${esc(...)}`.
triage.ceiling: TEXT PIN, and the wording below is deliberate — this field has been rewritten twice (PR #53 rounds 1 and 2) because both earlier versions claimed a property of the PROGRAM and a reviewer falsified each inside one round. A green run asserts that src/sec10k/web/static/index.html contains, verbatim modulo whitespace: every mention of `it.confidence` inside an interpolation whose whole `${...}` is the pinned marker, immediately followed by the pinned qualifier; exactly one declaration of each pinned helper, each with a body byte-equal to its pin; the pinned banner assignment, assignment target included; and the pinned coverage-strip wording with none of the forbidden wording. It does NOT assert that the page renders a qualified confidence, and no static read of one file could — these pins constrain the text a program is written in, not the program. Out of reach today, concretely: a number rendered without mentioning `it.confidence` (copied into a local first, or read off a re-shaped object); markup injected by another script or served from another file; anything hidden by CSS or never reached at runtime for a reason the text does not show — `#coverage{display:none}` keeps every pin here green while the banner says nothing, the same pin-mechanism hole `ui-exclusion-note`'s ceiling states. THAT LIST IS ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT EXHAUSTIVE: a text pin cannot enumerate the programs it fails to constrain, so read green as 'the pinned text is present and unique', never as 'the defect is impossible'. Separately and by design, `coverageStrip` only fires when `unattributed_content` fired, so a document below UNATTRIBUTED_MAX shows no line at all — the figure would have to be computed to be shown, and computing one in the display layer is the envelope change D8 owns. What the screen actually showed is tasks/reviews/d7-browser-walk.json; the falsification attempts run against these pins are tasks/reviews/pr53_mutation_probe.py.
